findings.summary: The new Remove block affordance says either party may remove a block, but the operation it invokes and the Block entity invariant both say only the blocker may remove it.
findings.evidence: affordance.ConnectionPanel.unblock effects: "Either party to the block may remove it" vs operation.block.remove preconditions: "Caller is the blocker" / failure: "Any caller other than the blocker is denied" and entity.Block invariant "Only the blocker can remove it"

findings.summary: The affordance's availability precondition and failure condition let a blocked person see Remove block, but the operation will always deny that person.
findings.evidence: affordance preconditions: "A block exists between the owner and this contact's linked account"; failure: "Not available when no block exists" — no blocker-only condition, while operation.block.remove requires "Caller is the blocker"

findings.summary: Remove block deletes the Block but never updates the Connection whose state was set to blocked, so that Connection's state after unblocking is undefined.
findings.evidence: entity.Connection state: "enum active|disconnected|blocked"; operation.block.remove links write only entity.Block and entity.RelationshipGoal, and its effects say "Delete the Block" with no Connection transition
